session_read: Two unrelated shocks hit the same session: SanDisk's Q1 guide missed consensus at the midpoint despite a Q4 beat, triggering a memory-sector reset (WDC -16%, SNDK, MU, Seagate, the DRAM ETF all down) that spilled into the Asian session overnight -- KOSPI -5% intraday, Samsung -6%, SK Hynix -8 to -10%. Separately, Celestica announced a $3B dilutive stock offering and fell -12.9%, still held, no stop fired. That combination triggered a 7-position stop-loss cascade within a 2.5-minute window right at the open -- EWY, NBIS, TER, QBTS, CIEN, GLW, COHR -- most filling near the session's opening lows before the broader tape (and several of those very names) recovered through the morning. The equity-only headline (-20%) is misleading: total book (equity+cash) is down a more modest -2.67% since this morning, because ~$6,000 of that 'lost' equity simply became cash. Drawdown deepened to -5.83% from peak, cash spiked to 25.3% (post_stop_event regime, correctly not flagged as a breach), and true AI-capex exposure held at 94.7% even after SKHY's classification. QBTS reported earnings today and gapped down ~14% before recovering to -9% -- a real result, not spillover.
